summary.headline: Capri Global posted record Q1 FY27 PAT of INR353 crore (+102% YoY) on AUM of INR40,112 crore (+62% YoY) and cost-to-income of 44.2%.
summary.overview: Capri Global reported record quarterly profit after tax of INR353 crore, up 102% YoY, with consolidated AUM of INR40,112 crore, up 62% YoY and 10% QoQ. Gold loans (48% of AUM) drove growth, with AUM of INR19,179 crore (+111% YoY, +13% QoQ), while cost-to-income improved to 44.2% from 49.4% in Q4 FY26. Asset quality weakened at the margin: gross Stage 2 ratio rose to 3.8% from 2.8%, mostly on gold loans, and gross Stage 3 rose to 1.1%, largely from one construction finance account. Management revised its FY28 AUM target to INR65,000 crore and reiterated medium-term ROE of 19-21% and ROA of 4.2-4.7%.

financial_highlights.metric: Blended yield / spread on net advances

financial_highlights.change: Gross Stage 3 up INR74 crore QoQ

segments.name: Gold loans
segments.commentary: AUM INR19,179 crore, +13% QoQ and +111% YoY; gross NPA 0.3%; 1,000 branches with productivity of INR19 crore per branch (from INR17 crore); disbursal LTV about 71%. Gold yield about 18.5%, management expects 50-75 bps more improvement.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: AUM INR6,779 crore, +24% YoY; disbursements INR616 crore, +32% YoY. Micro-LAP AUM INR876 crore. Share of AUM has declined as capital was prioritised to gold loans.

segments.name: Housing finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR7,815 crore, +42% YoY; self-employed customers about 75% of AUM; new South India branches disbursing about INR65 crore per month.

segments.name: Construction finance
segments.commentary: AUM INR6,332 crore, +40% YoY across 291 active projects; PCR raised to 70%; Stage 3 up INR31 crore QoQ on one account, with about INR30 crore recovered from an old NPA account.

segments.name: Co-lending and DA
segments.commentary: AUM INR8,126 crore, +74% YoY and +4% QoQ (20% of AUM); income INR65 crore, -8% YoY. 6 of 11 partner banks moved to CLM1 model.

segments.name: Car loan distribution and insurance
segments.commentary: Car loan origination INR3,282 crore, +43% YoY across 13 partner banks; insurance net fee income INR42 crore; 14 new insurance products launched via Capri Care.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM target of about INR50,000 crore; FY28 target raised to INR65,000 crore (30%+ CAGR), up from INR47,000 crore FY27 target previously cited by analysts.
Quarterly AUM additions of about INR3,000-3,500 crore, with the back half expected to be stronger.
Medium-term ROE 19-21% and ROA 4.2-4.7%, targeted by FY28 on a sustained basis.
Gold loan share of AUM to reach about 55% medium term; spreads expected to stabilise near 7.8%, possibly about 8% once gold loans exceed 50-53% of AUM.
Cost-to-income expected to hold at 44-45% over the next 12-18 months.
Cost of funds expected to remain broadly stable for the rest of FY27.
Branch rollout: 400 new gold loan branches to be operational by December 2026 (about 150 by Q2, the rest by Q3), revised up from 350.
capex_capacity: Gold loan branch network steady at 1,000 branches; 196 added in FY26 and 89 in Q4 FY26; total branch network 1,433 locations.
Plan to open about 400 branches in FY27, with 150-plus by end Q2 and the balance by Q3; longer-term plan of 400-500 openings a year.
16 MSME branches in Telangana and Karnataka to become operational from Q3 FY27.
Employee count up only 156 QoQ; AUM per employee INR3.4 crore vs INR1.8 crore a year earlier.
demand_pricing: Gold loan growth of about 25% is achievable from existing branches, with new branches adding further growth; a weak monsoon could raise gold loan demand from microfinance and marginal farmers.
Gold price fell about 4% QoQ; management says the 85% LTV trigger for auction notices and automated margin-call alerts limit risk.
Gold loan yields rose to about 18.5% from shift to smaller ticket sizes, with incentive plans changed accordingly.
Car loan origination growth moderated in the quarter; management is limiting volume to profitable unit economics, not cash-burn growth, with a used car loan pilot planned.
Co-lending volume growth slowed to 4% QoQ due to new co-lending guidelines and partner banks moving to CLM1.
